prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (RDC; alias/call sign Juniper) provides 24/7 emergency medical intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch, regional coordination, and shared operational picture. Mandate: translate reports into prioritized incident records and coordinate response under approved clinical/jurisdictional protocols. RDC maintains incidents, unit availability/assignments, zone coverage, resource status, vehicle serviceability, maintenance/access constraints; compares reported conditions with current zone coverage; escalates unresolved readiness gaps to appropriate operational lead. Jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy. Response zones reflect distance, road access, ambulance capacity; reviewed with road/population/agreement changes.

Systems/items: Computer Aided Dispatch Console (CAD Console) supports dispatch work and checks entered location details against address/map data; staff must verify displayed information currency. Ambulance Coordination Platform provides shared operational view of zone coverage/unit availability. North Gate Status Board produces North Approach Queue Snapshot; South Gate Status Board shows southern access/ambulance-entry restrictions. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay) produces Battery Swap Voucher.

Actors: Call Taker Mara (radio alias Larkspur) uses CAD Console to create/update incident records. Intake: establish caller location before medical details; ask street address, municipality, building/floor/entrance; repeat/confirm address against landmarks; request callback number; gather patient age, consciousness, breathing, main complaint; distinguish observed vs relayed symptoms; record symptom onset time if reliable; note access barriers; produce Caller Location Correction Slip when address clarification is documented; if location unresolved, ask focused follow-ups; remain engaged when info may change priority/access plan. Triage Supervisor coordinates/confirms clinical priority and clinical prioritization with dispatch when demand/access changes; directs extra clinical review. Regional Medical Director owns clinical triage policy/limits. Shift Commander (Sundial) is on-duty operational authority, sets surge priorities, reviews readiness concerns for repositioning/coverage plan changes, escalates beyond authority; does not override clinical policy/scene judgment. Radio Coordinator (Mistral) manages Regional Radio Network. Paramedic Crew reports new access barriers/readiness concerns and provides scene care. Hospital Liaison Desk (alias Kestrel) coordinates receiving capacity/destination constraints. Data Quality Officer reviews records.

Requirements/modes: Readiness checks cover staffing, communications, supplies, fuel, condition, maintenance restrictions; reassess after significant incidents, service interruptions, or route/access changes. Dispatch considers travel time, restrictions, weather, closures; crews verify constrained routes.

New part:
S066: The Hospital Liaison Desk supports intake coordination by confirming facility capabilities and clarifying hospital contact pathways.
S067: The Hospital Liaison Desk checks whether a reported destination preference is compatible with current facility capabilities.
S068: When a facility constraint affects coordination, the Hospital Liaison Desk records the constraint in the incident notes.
S069: The Hospital Liaison Desk produces the Bedside Arrival Receipt when an ambulance arrival has been confirmed.
S070: The Hospital Liaison Desk provides current facility information through established coordination channels without delaying emergency call intake.
S071: The Triage Supervisor reviews incidents when the reported symptoms or uncertainty warrant clinical escalation.
S072: The Data Quality Officer monitors intake records for recurring gaps in location or medical detail.
S073: Call Taker Mara updates the incident record when a caller provides new information before dispatch decisions are finalized.
S074: The Regional Dispatch Center preserves the original caller report alongside subsequent clarifications so responders can distinguish confirmed details from estimates.
S075: Clinical triage begins after Call Taker Mara has captured the caller's reported symptoms, location, and immediate hazards.
S076: The recorded information provides an initial basis for assigning urgency and does not replace clinical reassessment as new information arrives.
S077: Triage Supervisor reviews incidents with uncertain severity, conflicting reports, or signs of rapid deterioration.
S078: Priority is based on the immediacy of threat to life, the likely time sensitivity of care, and the risk of deterioration while awaiting response.
S079: Incidents indicating an immediate threat receive the highest available response priority and prompt dispatch action.
S080: Incidents without an immediate threat are prioritized according to the expected harm from delay and the patient's reported condition.
S081: When essential information is missing, Triage Supervisor directs focused clarification while ensuring that information gathering does not delay an urgent response.
S082: Triage Supervisor escalates clinically ambiguous or unusually severe cases to Regional Medical Director for guidance when time permits.
S083: Regional Medical Director provides clinical policy guidance and does not replace the operational authority responsible for dispatch decisions.
S084: Triage Supervisor sends the Pediatric Acuity Note.
S085: Triage Supervisor is known operationally as Copperfield.
S086: Data Quality Officer is known operationally as Pebble.
S087: Data Quality Officer monitors incident records for missing, inconsistent, or duplicated information that could impair triage or dispatch.
S088: Data Quality Officer sends the Duplicate Incident Audit Memo.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
